DESCRIPTION: How Orbitline sessions keep every replica in step without a central server: a technical brief on the (fictional) sync protocol.
DOC_TITLE: Merging without a referee: the Orbitline sync protocol
DOC_SUBTITLE: Every buffer is a CRDT, so collaborators and agents converge on the same text by identifier, not by position, and no server has to decide who typed first.
SUMMARY: A session is a set of replicas of the same buffers. Each replica applies its own edits at once and integrates remote ones by identifier, so all of them end with the same text.
CALLOUT_BODY: Input never waits on the network. Merging happens after the keystroke is on screen, never before.
PRINCIPLE_1_BODY: Each character carries a globally unique, totally ordered identifier; an insert names the character it follows.
PRINCIPLE_2_BODY: A delete hides a character instead of removing it, and compaction runs once every replica has seen the delete.
CARD_1_BODY: Applied immediately to the local replica and stamped with the next clock value.
CARD_2_BODY: Sent directly to every participant; the relay only helps peers find each other.
CARD_3_BODY: Every replica sorts by (clock, replica) and reads the same text.
ROW_1_C: Character on screen in the same frame
SECTION_2_LEAD: A new participant catches up from a snapshot and the operations after it, then edits like everyone else.
STEP_1_BODY: The owner's replica sends the current buffer and its clock.
STEP_2_BODY: Operations newer than the snapshot are applied in identifier order.
STEP_3_BODY: The participant receives a replica number and starts typing.
CODE_COMMENT: Join a session and watch it converge
CLOSING_STATEMENT: Choosing a data structure is choosing where you are willing to pay for complexity.
NEXT_BODY: Share a single file with one collaborator before inviting agents into a whole project.
BOUNDARY_BODY: Convergence is automatic; keeping a change is not. Review stays a deliberate step for the people involved.
FOOTNOTE: Orbitline is a fictional product used to demonstrate gridline-style. Nothing in this brief is a real measurement.
